newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Chemunex says Hoechst OKs system.
newsitem.headline: Chemunex says Hoechst OKs system.

text.p: French microbiology firm Chemunex said an evaluation by Hoechst Marion Roussel of its laser scanning-based system ChemScan confirmed the new system was well suited for routine microbiological water analysis.
Hoechst Marion Roussel is a unit of German pharmaceuticals and chemicals group Hoechst AG.

Chemunex develops and markets rapid testing systems for microbe contamination mainly for the pharmaceuticals, water and food industries. The company was listed on European growth stocks market Easdaq in March.

In the four-month evaluation of ChemScan, Hoechst found that filtration, labelling and analysis were achievable with 90 minutes compared to the two to five day incubation period needed for the conventional plate count method, Chemunex said in a statement.
Chemunex said the report provided further evidence of the system's potential to achieve significant cost savings in the pharmaceutical industry.
